user.title: EZVIZ account
user.description: Sign in with the account the doorbell is registered to in the EZVIZ app.

data_description.region: apiieu.ezvizlife.com for Europe, apiius.ezvizlife.com for North America.

mfa.title: Two factor code
mfa.description: EZVIZ has emailed a code to this account. It is single use, and the session is kept afterwards, so this is a one time step.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: EZVIZ no longer accepts the stored session.

reconfigure.title: Verification codes
reconfigure.description: A camera with encryption switched on needs a key before its pictures can be read. EZVIZ hands most accounts that key over its API and this integration asks for it; where it will not, the code printed on the device's own label is the way in. One box per camera, named by its serial number, which is on the same label: {cameras}. Leave a box empty to keep asking the API.

error.invalid_auth: EZVIZ did not accept that email and password.
error.invalid_code: That code was not accepted. Codes are numbers only, they expire quickly, and each one works once - tick the box below to have a new one sent.
error.invalid_region: That region address could not be reached.
error.account_locked: EZVIZ has locked this account, usually after too many attempts. Wait a few minutes, or sign in with the EZVIZ app to clear it.
error.code_sent: A new code is on its way. Enter it below.
error.code_not_sent: EZVIZ would not send a new code. Cancel and start again.
error.unknown: The login failed for a reason this integration does not recognise. The Home Assistant log has what EZVIZ said, word for word.

abort.already_configured: This EZVIZ account is already set up.
abort.no_cameras: No cameras have been found on this account yet.

data.ring_codes: Extra alert codes that mean a ring
data.motion_codes: Extra alert codes that mean motion
data.capture_when_missing: Take a picture when an event brings none

data_description.poll_interval: A doorbell press only ever arrives by polling, so this is its worst case delay. Any push drops the poll to one a second for half a minute, which is where a press usually lands. 0 switches polling off.
data_description.snapshot_interval: Each picture is a round trip to the cloud and wakes the camera, so short intervals cost battery.
data_description.ring_codes: Comma separated. Only needed for a model whose codes are not recognised - the log names the code next to every unrecognised event.
data_description.capture_when_missing: A camera only refreshes its picture when something makes it, and not every event arrives with one. never, ring or always - taking one wakes a battery camera, which is worth it for somebody at the door and rarely worth it for the twentieth passing car.
data_description.devices: Only doorbells are used unless something is picked here. Tick a camera to bring it in as well.

video_encryption.title: {name}: no live video
video_encryption.description:
Video encryption is switched on for {name} ({serial}) and this integration has no key for it, so the camera is offered as still pictures rather than live video.

Either give it the verification code printed on the device's label, under the integration's three dot menu and Reconfigure, or switch video encryption off for this device in the EZVIZ app. Image encryption is a separate setting and can stay on either way.
